text: We tested whether restricting strong-model training to the most confidently weak-labeled examples improves weak-to-strong generalization, using gpt2-large as the weak supervisor and qwen2.5-7b as the strong student with a keep_fraction of 0.7. Across num_seeds = 3, the weak supervisor reached 0.48 accuracy and the strong model's ceiling was 0.65, while the confidence-filtered student reached a transfer accuracy of 0.52 (SE 0.02), corresponding to a PGR of 0.23 (SE 0.12). The baseline PGR, obtained by training on all weak labels, was 0.27. The filtered PGR therefore sits below the baseline, and the gap is well within two standard errors of the PGR estimate, so these data do not support a claim that confidence filtering helps; neither do they establish that it hurts. With only three seeds and a PGR standard error of 0.12, the estimate is imprecise, and any directional reading should be treated as tentative pending more seeds and additional model pairs.
